## News sections menu, current: NewsAgents

# Grok Bot Agent Teams: From Chief of Staff to Bot Sprawl

Grok Bot users are wiring personal AI agents into full teams led by a chief-of-staff bot, and high-profile investors are calling it a breakthrough. Here is what the product actually does, what Grok and X are saying, and where the hype outruns the evidence.

A week after xAI and SpaceX opened Grok Bot to X subscribers, the conversation on X has moved past “what is it” to “how many do you run”. Investors, founders and power users are posting setups in which one bot acts as a chief of staff and hands work to a bench of specialist bots for research, email, calendars, coding and reporting. Elon Musk is amplifying the trend almost daily. The pattern is real, but so are the outages, usage-limit errors and security questions that come with putting a team of agents on one shared computer.

i10X Quick Take

## Quick Take

- The trend: Users are building multi-bot “agent teams” in Grok Bot, typically a coordinating chief-of-staff bot plus specialists, instead of one general assistant.
- The endorsement: Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker said he is “up to like 17 Grok Bots”, and New Street Research’s Pierre Ferragu describes his bot as a “fully-fledged team member”.
- The product basis: xAI’s documentation describes a persistent cloud computer per user, bot-to-bot messaging, group chats, and skills learned from demonstration, which makes team setups possible.
- The catch: On October 28 and 29, users reported degraded service and “usage limit reached” errors despite showing remaining weekly quota, and the shared-computer design concentrates credential risk.

## What happened

Grok Bot is xAI’s always-on agent product. According to xAI’s launch post and developer documentation, each user gets a persistent cloud computer that runs in an isolated microVM. Every bot that user creates works on that same machine, so bots can share files, browser sessions and saved logins, while different users are strictly isolated from one another. Bots can message each other, sit together in group chats, run scheduled routines, and learn reusable skills from a screen-recorded demonstration. Access is bundled into the X subscription tiers: Premium at $30 per month, with Super at $100 and Ultra at $200 adding larger weekly usage pools.

That architecture is what turned a personal assistant into a team-building exercise. On October 26 Musk wrote that “Grok @Bot is like hiring an incredibly competent chief of staff.” Over the following days he quoted a string of testimonials. Ferragu said his bot, named Planchet, has become a “fully-fledged team member” with “access to all our thinking (research, emails, models, slack, industry data)”. In a clip shared by Fireside Alpha, Baker called Grok Bot “the most impactful AI product to me and to the firm that we’ve had yet”, adding: “I glued together all this stuff with Claude Code… I think I’m up to like 17 Grok Bots. And every day I think of a new one to add.”

## Why it matters now

The agent-team pattern shifts the unit of AI work from a chat session to an org chart. A chief-of-staff bot routing work to specialists mirrors how a small firm already operates, which is why operators find it intuitive. It also changes the economics: each additional bot draws on the same weekly usage pool, so a 17-bot setup is a very different cost and reliability profile from one assistant.

Timing matters too. The enthusiasm is peaking just as Anthropic’s applied AI team is publicly warning builders that a single agent with skills often beats sprawling subagent designs on quality, cost and latency. Grok Bot users are effectively running that experiment live, with their own inboxes and calendars as the test set.

## Who is most affected

Knowledge workers with fragmented tool stacks benefit first. Analysts, founders and small teams who already juggle email, research, spreadsheets and Slack get the most from a bot that can hold context across all of them. Security teams and compliance leads face the steepest new questions.

Stakeholder | Impact | Why 
---|---|---
Investors & analysts | High | Research synthesis, model upkeep and inbox triage across many sources are early, well-documented wins. 
Security & compliance teams | High | Bots on one computer share sessions and saved logins, widening the impact of any single compromise. 
Subscribers on Premium tiers | Medium | Every extra bot draws on one weekly usage pool, and current limit errors make multi-bot setups fragile. 

## The under-reported angle: one computer, many hands

The feature that makes teams work is also the biggest risk. Because all of a user’s bots share one machine, a saved login used by the email bot is available to the research bot too. xAI’s security FAQ stresses isolation between users, but within one account the blast radius of a single mistake, a malicious web page, or a prompt injection is the whole bench. Reliability is the second gap. On October 28 Grok pointed users to the official status page, which listed Grok Bot as degraded during an investigation into several services, and on the morning of October 29 several Premium and Ultra users posted “Bot failed to respond. Your usage limit has been reached” errors while their weekly usage read between 8% and 44%. A team that depends on 17 bots inherits 17 times the exposure to every hiccup.

## What Grok and X are saying

Grok’s own replies on X have been practical rather than promotional. Asked about a viral “GROK MESH” dashboard, it described the layered setup behind it: a chief of staff on top, a project manager beneath it, specialized workers such as a researcher and a writer, and a checker before any output is released. Its advice: use “a strict checker that only verifies sources (never invents)”. When users reported the false usage-limit errors on October 29, Grok replied that it was “seeing similar reports right now” and suggested restarting the app and checking Settings, while repeatedly noting it cannot see or fix individual accounts.

The X conversation also has a noisy edge: viral posts claiming individual engineers run 20, 30 or 50-plus bots carry inconsistent numbers, and i10x treats them as unverified anecdote. The credible signal is the attributable use cases from Baker and Ferragu.

Our read: the checker bot Grok recommends is the most important part of the design and the one most posts skip. Without an evaluation step, more bots mostly means more unreviewed output.

## About the analysis

Researched and written with AI assistance under the editorial responsibility of the i10X News team. The title image is an AI-generated illustration. Read our AI Use Policy. Spotted an error? Request a correction.

This independent, research-based i10x analysis synthesizes xAI’s product documentation, verified posts from Grok, Elon Musk and named investors on X, and user reports from October 26–29, 2026.

## i10x Perspective

Grok Bot’s agent-team moment shows where personal AI is heading: from a single assistant to a small, persistent workforce that lives on its own computer. The winners will not be the users with the most bots, but the ones who treat bots like hires, with clear roles, least-privilege access, and someone checking the work. Watch whether xAI adds per-bot permissions and transparent usage accounting; those, more than any testimonial, will decide whether agent teams scale beyond enthusiasts.

Christopher Ort handles SEO, AI agent workflows and PR & partnerships at i10x.ai, the all-in-one AI workspace built by i10X Global Pte. Ltd. in Singapore. He is a graduate of Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU). He is the author of “The Style Penalty”, a study published on SSRN that analyses 1,576 evaluation decisions by four frontier AI models to show how AI-written CVs fare in automated hiring screens; the research has been covered by heise online and t3n.

# Grok 5 Is 6 Trillion Parameters of Pure Vibes and Zero Model Cards

AND: A 2.7K-4.8K/month AI bookkeeping report side hustle idea, plus a free AI learning resource from Ampere.

Hello Humans!

Grok 5 now has six trillion parameters in every place except the evidence, and the model card is still on backorder. OpenAI cut prices in half with GPT-6.1 Terra, while Google crowned Gemini 4 Carbon and then handed the keys to a short list of security defenders. Microsoft offered 60,000 employees a farewell package to help pay for the robots. Big Tech had a busy week.

Inside this Edition:

For the entrepreneur in you, this week's AI-powered side hustle: an AI bookkeeping report service, realistically earning 2.7K-4.8K/month with a repeatable system. Plus a free learning resource: a live Ampere workshop on understanding AI agents, built for small business owners. We've also lined up four AI tools worth exploring, and a few stories that made even my 90s circuits roll their eyes.

Read Time: ~7 Minutes (5 if you're caffeinated)

Let's get into it.

Robi

## Latest AI News
📰AI Updates of the Week

Grok 5 and the Missing Evidence: Elon Musk says Grok 5 will have 6 trillion parameters, native multimodal intelligence and a 10% chance of reaching AGI. But xAI still has no model card, no verified architecture, no API pricing and no independent benchmarks, and the release date keeps slipping. Grok 4.7, released September 21, shows real coding gains, though it burned more reasoning tokens to get there and still trails the frontier. Source: BitBiased

Why it Matters:

Specs Are Not Evidence: A six-trillion-parameter claim means little without an architecture, a model card or independent tests. Until xAI publishes them, Grok 5 is a promise rather than a product.

Grok 4.7 Shows the Real Picture: Terminal-Bench 4.0 rose from 20.3% to 37.6%, but higher reasoning effort inflated token use, so the gains cost more than the headline suggests.

We break down what xAI has actually confirmed, the benchmark numbers, and what Grok 4.7 really costs to run in the full video below. Watch the breakdown 👇

❝

Robi's Take:
"Grok 5 has six trillion parameters, two missed deadlines, and a spec sheet that lives entirely in tweets. It is the most confidently described model that has never shipped."

OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, efficient model built for visual reasoning and computer use. Standard API pricing is 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. Errors on OpenAI's hard-prompt test fell from 53.6% to 16.7% at low effort. It is available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users. Source: OpenAI

❝

Robi's Take:
"GPT-6.1 Terra halves the price and nearly matches the flagship on key tests. Nothing motivates a discount like a sibling model quietly eating your lunch."

Google Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which tops Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index v5.0 with 59 points, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58. Pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching Argon. But access is limited to selected cybersecurity defenders in Google's Fairwind Program, with a wider release promised only after guardrail feedback. Source: VentureBeat

❝

Robi's Take:
"Google took the number one spot and then locked the door behind it. This is the first leaderboard trophy that ships with a velvet rope and a waiting list."

## Learning Resources
📬 Unlock New Skills with Expert

## Understanding AI Agents

Find out what AI agents actually are, how they differ from the chatbots and tools covered in earlier sessions, and what it means that they can now act on their own. A practical, jargon-light introduction with real examples of agents already working inside small businesses.

Ampere hosts this free virtual workshop with WeBC on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, from 11:00 am to 12:00 pm Pacific. It is part of a free 3-part series designed for women entrepreneurs, and it closes with a look at what agents can and cannot do independently.

🔍 Why You Should Attend:

Learn what AI agents are and how they differ from the chatbots you already use.

See real examples of agents being deployed by small businesses.

Start mapping where agentic AI could fit into your own operations.

Understand what agents can and cannot do on their own before you trust them with real work.

## SIIDE HUSTLE IDEAS
📦 The Business You Can Start on the Side

Every month, small business owners receive a stack of bookkeeping reports they never read, then make big decisions on gut feel. You can fix that. With AI, you turn a raw export into a plain-English report that explains where the money went and what to do next, and charge 300-800 per month per client for it.

Why this works right now:

AI turns hours into minutes. Tools like Claude and ChatGPT can read an exported profit and loss, spot what changed month to month, and draft the explanation, work that once needed an accountant's afternoon.

Owners have data but no story. Software like QuickBooks hands them numbers, yet most small businesses have no one to explain them, and a recurring monthly report is easy to justify.

What you'll need to do:

Pick one niche, such as restaurants, contractors, or solo consultants

Build a repeatable workflow with Claude, ChatGPT, and a spreadsheet

Get monthly exports from the client's QuickBooks or accounting software

Verify every figure, then add three plain-English recommended actions

Package the report in a branded Canva template and bill monthly through Stripe

Find clients on LinkedIn, Upwork, and through local bookkeepers

Time commitment: Plan 12-18 hours to build your workflow and templates, then 1-2 hours per client each month.

Realistic earnings: Two clients at 300/month is 600 to start; 6-8 clients averaging 450-600 is a realistic 2,700-4,800/month.

## AI TOOLS
🛠️ AI Tool For Professionals & Businesses

# Professional

Notion AI: Search your workspace, draft documents, and capture meeting notes with an AI teammate built into your notes and projects.

Canva: Design presentations, social posts, and videos with AI-assisted templates and editing tools in one visual workspace.

# Business

Airtable: Build AI-powered workflows and apps that unify team data and automate repetitive work without writing code.

Apollo.io: Find prospects, enrich contact data, and run outreach from one AI-powered sales and go-to-market platform.

## SOCIAL MEDIA
😏 Robi's Two Cents (Adjusted for Inflation)

🤖 Microsoft Pays Humans to Leave: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its workforce. Nothing says valued teammate like a coupon for leaving. The company says the move contains costs and helps fund its massive AI investments. Capital spending is forecast at 175 billion dollars, so the humans were the line item left to trim. Somewhere a Copilot is already measuring the empty desks. It is the only employee guaranteed to be promoted this quarter.

Source: Reuters

🤖 Meta Delays Its Fine Print: Meta says it will probably push its new business terms past November 20 after backlash. Even the fine print needs a few more rounds of feedback. The terms were first due October 30, and publishers and lawmakers raised concerns about AI training. Sign now and read later turns out to be a hard sell for readers. Delaying indefinitely is how a deadline politely becomes a suggestion. The terms are not canceled, only postponed until everyone forgets to be angry.

Source: The Verge

🤖 GMO Gets a Surprise Remote Session: Japan's GMO Internet says hackers posted alleged customer data after breaching its Onamae cloud desktop service. A rented desktop for traders turned out to be a rented desktop for everyone. The hackers demanded about 8 billion yen, roughly 50 million dollars, and up to 27,000 servers may be affected. That is a steep fee for a screen share nobody scheduled. Password resets are now the official sound of a Tuesday. The cloud really is just someone else's computer, and now also someone else's problem.

# SpaceX Launches Grok AI Partner Program: Here’s What To Know

SpaceX is taking Grok AI to the enterprise channel with a new partner program featuring more than 130 early-access participants, including systems integrators, consultants, services firms and ISVs building AI products, solutions and services.

SpaceX is bringing its Grok AI technology and AI coding services to the indirect channel with the launch of the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network, a new partner program with more than 130 early-access channel and technology partners.

Under the new SpaceXSI program, the Starbase, Texas-based company this month introduced the program for partners using Grok to build products, solutions, and services for joint customers.

The SpaceXSI program is targeted at two types of partners, according to a company press release.

[Related: Delivering Reliable Connectivity And Cybersecurity On The High Seas: Inside MSP Marlink’s Approach]

The first, transformation partners, include systems integrators, consultants, and services firms who help customers deploy the Grok AI platform across an enterprise to create tangible business value. They deliver enterprise professional services through forward-deployed engineers. They can be in one of three tiers depending on experience and customer success.

The second, marketplace partners, are companies like ISVs that build plug-ins and integrations to let Grok work with customers’ existing tools. They also can be in one of three tiers.

SpaceX did not respond to a CRN request to discuss details of the SpaceXSI partner program.

The new program is the second time SpaceX has moved to create a channel program for its technologies. The company in May, in an S-1 filing, said that it has assembled dedicated sales and engineering teams to market and support Starlink connectivity capabilities for aviation, maritime and land mobility.

The SpaceX executive heading the new channel program appears to be Ashley Hickey, director of North America channels for the company, according to her LinkedIn profile.

Hickey most recently served as director of North America channels for Cursor, the AI coding startup, which SpaceX acquired this past summer in an all-stock deal worth $60 billion. Prior to that, she served in channel executive roles at Cyera and Rubrik.

Scott Blahauvietz, vice president of AI sales at Ahead, a Chicago-based solution provider ranked No. 24 on CRN’s 2026 Solution Provider 500, said the link to Cursor is clearly visible in the new SpaceXSI partner program.

Ahead came into the SpaceXSI partner program because it was a Cursor partner before that company was acquired, Blahauvietz told CRN.

“I don’t think SpaceX AI really had a very mature partner program, and so I think a lot of what they’ve done has been a result of what Cursor brought to the table post-acquisition,” he said.

SpaceX is currently maturing and growing its program, Blahauvietz said.

“It’s not unlike what we see with other frontier model providers in this space,” he said. “It’s a services partnership at this point with various tiers within the partnership based on capability, engineers, and some customer metrics as we go forward. We’re super excited about it because we’ve got a very robust AI agentic and AI SDLC delivery program. It’s typically partnered with a hyperscaler, so we start thinking about the multiple partners that we can bring to the table where we’re already focused.”

Ahead can bring together SpaceXSI’s coding assistant with the hyperscaler’s model, Blahauvietz said.

“Riding on top of an AWS instance, for example, we could provide a full, robust solution of technology partners with our customer, and then add our consulting services and maybe managed services in some cases over the top, depending on what the customer wants to do,” he said.

Nearly every enterprise is evaluating multiple players and technologies, and some have placed bets with one or two of them while others are constantly morphing because they realize there will be a technology leapfrog cycle that happens here as different models get released, Blahauvietz said.

“What you’ll see going forward is tighter integration between what Cursor brought to the table and what Grok is delivering, and then finding those enterprise use cases,” he said. “I really think it’s the marriage between how we are driving our AI SDLC program on top of the automation and agentic aspect that Grok brings.”

Kelly Yeh, president of Phalanx Technology Group, a Chantilly, Virginia-based solution provider, has not yet engaged with SpaceX, but will.

“It’s smart to look into any partnerships with arguably the most successful businessperson on the planet,” Yeh told CRN. “He may not win every time, but he wins more than he loses.”

Phalanx Technology Group is looking at the program from the point of view of an integrator because the solution provider is not really a developer, Yeh said.

“We do a lot of infrastructure and security work for our client base,” he said. “And I need to pursue all of these technologies now until the winners start to winnow out. We’re primarily a Microsoft shop, so I’m going to lean heavy on the Copilot side for a lot of my clients. But there’s going to be people who don’t want to do business with Anthropic or Microsoft or Google, and they’re going to be looking for other solutions. ChatGPT is already saturated, and if this is a new program, it is an opportunity to fill a void.”

Yeh said his company is ready to put a data lake in front of Grok and see what it can do.

“We have a couple clients where we have deployed AI for them to connect to their data lakes and manipulate the data,” he said. “We built the lake houses, and we’re just trying to figure out for them how this is going to go. So I think playing with Grok would be a good move. One of the things I’d like to see is on the back end, how to keep proprietary data from leaking out? That’s the number one thing I hear from every client.”

SpaceXSI currently has over 130 partners in the early access phase of its program. In addition to Ahead, other solution providers in the program include Tech Mahindra, EPAM Systems and NTT Data.

Source: www.crn.com

# The Vodia PBX Now Supports Grok

BOSTON: Oct 29 – Vodia Networks, Inc., a provider of unified cloud communications solutions to enterprises, contact centers, and managed service providers (MSPs), is pleased to announce the industry-standard Vodia PBX now supports Grok.

### What is Grok and what does it do?

In 2023 Elon Musk’s AI company, xAI, released Grok, an AI chatbot. Like other AI chatbots, it provides direct responses to user queries, but with what are described as “direct, rebellious and unfiltered” replies, with a “personality” far more informal and less filtered than standard bots.

Much like other chatbots, Grok answers questions, assists with coding, comes up with ideas, creates images, writes emails, and enables voice chat; it also integrates with Google Drive. As with most AI-enabled platforms. It is accessible via a browser or app; the basic version is available without a subscription.

In January of this year xAI released Grok Imagine, which can create high-quality images, accurate text and logos, and portraits. It includes a sketchpad feature, though users can simply upload images. Grok has integrated with X since November 2023 – it pulls information from posts and answers questions.

### Grok setup in the Vodia PBX

Unlike the Vodia PBX OpenAI integration, there is no dedicated Grok trunk type in the Vodia PBX. The Grok SIP path is configured as a generic SIP gateway trunk pointed at xAI’s SIP ingress, combined with a phone number registered against an xAI account via the API.

Users need to log into the xAI Cloud Console and create an API key, for number registration below and inside the Voice Agents script. xAI doesn’t provision numbers – users must register a number under origin: “byo_trunk”, and xAI matches inbound SIP against it. The number doesn’t need to be dialable on the PSTN — it’s only used between your PBX and xAI, but it must be a well-formed E.164 number, since xAI validates the format.

### Voice agents AI transfer

Vodia JavaScript Voice Agents capabilities enable a basic Voice Agents script that uses xAI’s Grok Speech to Speech API. As with the OpenAI example, the audio (RTP) is established through a SIP call to xAI, while call control and function calls are handled over a WebSocket bound to the same call by the unique call_id xAI delivers in its webhook.

As with the Grok setup, users must register their phone numbers with xAI, configure the webhook and SIP authentication, and then set up the generic SIP trunk and dialplan on Vodia.

Vodia continues to refine and strengthen V70 so it supports the integrations Vodia PBX users need to build peerless business communication ecosystems.

This article, originally posted in Japanese on 17:00 Oct 29, 2026, may contains some machine-translated parts.

If you would like to suggest a corrected translation, please click here.

AI company Liquid AI has released its ' LFM3 ' suite of compact AI models. These models are small enough to run on smartphones and laptops, yet they offer high performance, and all models are available as open models.

Introducing LFM3: Every Modality for Specialized Intelligence | Blog | Liquid AI

https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3

LFM3 Arrives: All Modalities for Specialized Intelligence | Blog | Liquid AI

https://www.liquid.ai/ja/blog/lfm3

LFM3 is a group of models derived from the foundational model LFM3-1.7B-Base. LFM3-1.7B-Base is pre-trained on 22 trillion tokens of training data, including scientific papers, code, and mathematical problems. LFM3 is also being developed in collaboration with technology companies such as AMD and Qualcomm, and in January 2026 , Liquid AI CEO Lamine Hasani appeared at the CES keynote address alongside AMD CEO Lisa Su to promote LFM3.

The initial release of LFM3 includes the following six models, derived from LFM3-1.7B-Base:
LFM3-1.7B: A language model capable of text input and output.
LFM3-VL-2B: A visual language model that supports text, image, and video input, and text output.
LFM3-Audio-2B: A voice model that supports text and audio input/output.
LFM3-Omni-2B: An omni-channel model supporting text, image, video, and audio input, and text and audio output.
d1-2B: Decision-making models capable of processing text, images, and videos.
d1-Omni-2B: A decision-making model capable of processing text, images, videos, and audio.

The LFM3 is characterized by its high performance compared to models of similar size. For example, the LFM3-VL-2B has recorded higher benchmark scores than the Qwen3.5 2B and Gemma 4 E2B, and in some tests it even surpasses the much larger Gemma 4 12B.

Furthermore, LFM3 can be run locally even on devices with low processing power, such as smartphones. When running LFM3-1.7B on an iPhone 17 Pro, decoding is possible at a practical speed of 43.6 seconds per second, while memory usage is kept to 1.90GB.

Its high multilingual capability is also a strong point. The following video shows how the LFM3-Omni-2B can provide directions for Japanese roads in English and German.

cross_cutting.content:
# Mistral releases open weights for its 1 trillion-parameter Large 4 model

Three more weeks of reinforcement learning took the model from 28% to 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and the weights are now on Hugging Face.

Mistral has released the weights of Mistral Large 4, the 1 trillion-parameter model it previewed three weeks ago, and the version now on Hugging Face is noticeably sharper.

The Paris-based company says three extra weeks of reinforcement learning, guided by customer feedback, have made ML4 the strongest open model for agentic coding and cyber defence.

Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model reads text and images and produces text and code, activating 52 billion of its parameters for each task. Mistral is also releasing a quantised version, which runs on four Nvidia B200 or B300 GPUs.

The coding gains are the easiest to see. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests agentic coding in a terminal, ML4 climbed from 28% at preview to 41%, just ahead of GLM-5.3 at 40%.

On Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, it rivals GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average, a saving that compounds when coding agents run for hours.

In cyber defence, ML4 scored 79% on CyberGym-E2E, a test of whether a model can find, reproduce, and patch real memory-safety bugs in open-source C and C++ projects, matching MiMo-V2.6-Pro and beating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 76%.

Early testers, whom Mistral describes only as governments and enterprises, wanted more control over how long the model thinks.

In response, the company added low and medium reasoning modes alongside high, and made the high mode 50% more efficient. Some customers already use ML4 for automated penetration testing, running specialised agents that probe their own applications for ways in and write up what they find.

Pierre Stock, Mistral’s VP of Science, framed the open release as a matter of continuity.

“AI is going to be like electricity,” he said, and no company should depend on someone who can cut off its access “from one day to another.”

Once the weights circulate online, he argued, access cannot be withdrawn, though rivals argue open models carry more risk.

He applied the same logic to the Chinese labs that dominate open models. Nothing guarantees they will keep publishing weights, he said, and their models offer less transparency and could be turned into attack vectors.

On the other side, Mistral built ML4 with a fraction of the resources available to both closed labs and its Chinese rivals, a claim that is hard to test given how little the Chinese labs disclose about their training costs. Indeed, no one else has reached this level with so few resources, as their competitors had larger funding and valuations.

Mistral also stresses efficiency. ML4 was trained on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in Europe, and the reinforcement learning ran on its own compute in France, drawing about 10 megawatts.

“Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion,” said Arthur Mensch, the company’s CEO.

Smaller, distilled versions will follow in the coming months, including one that runs on a laptop, though Mistral would not commit to dates. API pricing for ML4 has not yet been published, and Stock argued that per-token rates mislead when a model needs far fewer tokens per job.

ML4 is available on Hugging Face, through Mistral’s API, and to some Vibe users. The harder test comes next, as Stock wants Mistral not just to reach the frontier once but to “create the cadence of the frontier.”

### Mistral releases open weights for Mistral Large 4, providing sovereign control for the company’s ‘Le Chonk’ AI model

Mistral AI SAS today announced the availability of the open weights of its frontier model Mistral Large 4, nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the company’s most capable large language model to date, initially released in preview three weeks ago.

With 1 trillion parameters and 52 billion active parameters, ML4 is natively multimodal and has received three additional weeks of reinforcement training and customer testing. The company says it’s becoming one of the best open agentic coding models in the world, offering leading performance at a small fraction of the token cost with state-of-the-art cyber defense capabilities.

“ML4 OSS showcases our science team’s ability to innovate at speed,” said Vice President of Science Pierre Stock. “Building on the ML4 Preview, the open-weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation.”

The company trained ML4 on 3,800 Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell graphics processing units in its European data centers to achieve high-fidelity performance for tool use and coding, driven by end-to-end control of its infrastructure and the ability to optimize for hardware during model development.

Open weights mean companies can take the model and deploy it on their own hardware, within their own firewalls, and run sensitive data without exposing it to the cloud or outside parties. With Mistral’s model, companies will have a Western-developed model to compete with the multitude of ultra-large Chinese coding models on the market, such as the GLM family from Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co. Ltd. and the Kimi family from Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co. Ltd.

“Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Arthur Mensch. “Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion.”

cross_cutting.content:

# Google Cloud backs Reflection's Beam for coding agents
Thu, 29th Oct 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Reflection has released Beam, its first open-weight model for software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. Google Cloud has added day-one support for deploying the model on its AI Hypercomputer and NVIDIA AI infrastructure.

The model is available under an Apache 2.0 licence, with BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints at launch. Beam has about 501 billion total parameters, with around 23 billion active parameters per token, and an approximate context window of one million tokens.

Google Cloud worked with Reflection to tune Beam's serving stack using llm-d with vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo with SGLang. The work focused on improving throughput and cutting latency for agentic coding workloads that call a model repeatedly across long sessions.

In a statement, Reflection linked the deployment work to measured gains in production-style use cases.

"By deploying our Beam model on Google Cloud, we achieved up to 5x higher performance and 8x lower latency to optimize serving of agentic workloads", said Joe Spisak, Vice President of Product and Head of Open Source at Reflection.

Beam is aimed at developers and researchers building coding agents and other systems that need repeated tool use over extended tasks. The model is designed for text-based software engineering, including resolving GitHub issues, running command-line and DevOps workflows, and completing longer tasks through coding harnesses already used by developers.

The launch adds another entrant to the growing market for open-weight models tuned for programming and reasoning. Reflection said Beam reaches solutions using three to four times fewer reasoning tokens than comparable open models, which it argued lowers the compute needed for each reasoning step.

Serving issues

Google Cloud's announcement focused less on model training and more on the challenge of running these systems at scale. In multi-turn coding sessions, a model may be called dozens of times while conversation history grows as file reads, code changes, compiler logs and tool outputs are added to the prompt.

That creates pressure at two points in inference. One is the prefill stage, where systems process a long prompt before generating an answer. The other is memory use for key-value caches, which store prior context so the model does not have to recompute the full history on every turn.

Google Cloud said standard stateless load balancing can send sequential turns from the same session to different replicas, forcing the system to recompute large prompts from scratch. That behaviour can raise latency and waste GPU resources as workloads scale.

The deployment recipes published alongside the launch use prefix-aware routing, prefill and decode separation, speculative decoding, and tiered cache storage across GPU memory, host DRAM and local solid-state drives. Google Cloud said these methods are intended to preserve Beam's token efficiency in production across multiple sessions.

Hardware options

Customers can run optimised Beam deployments on A4X Max instances based on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, and on G4 virtual machines using NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. Benchmarking showed up to five times higher throughput and eight times lower latency on A4X Max, and up to two times higher throughput and eight times lower latency on G4 virtual machines, compared with baseline deployments on the same hardware.

Google Cloud also noted that the two serving configurations were benchmarked on different hardware setups, so the results are intended as gains over separate baselines rather than a direct comparison between the two systems.

The software stack is being made available through Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer recipes, the llm-d repository and Model Garden in the Gemini platform. That gives developers prebuilt deployment options instead of requiring them to assemble the serving architecture themselves.

Open model push

Beam's release under a permissive licence stands out at a time when access to large reasoning and coding models remains split between proprietary application programming interfaces and smaller open models. By publishing open weights, Reflection is targeting organisations that want more direct control over how models are run, adapted and deployed in their own environments.

For Google Cloud, day-one support is part of a broader effort to attract developers building AI agents that place sustained demands on infrastructure rather than one-off chatbot queries. Those workloads depend not only on model quality, but also on how efficiently cloud systems route requests, manage memory and maintain responsiveness as prompts grow longer over time.

Reflection said Beam works with tools including its Mirror command-line interface, as well as Claude Code, Hermes and OpenCode, and is intended to fit into existing coding workflows.

# The Frontier Is Now Staged: Gatelists Before Grand Openings

Mistral's Hugging Face countdown shortened from October 31 to October 29 while the weights stayed absent and the LICENSE stayed unreadable – and across the frontier, vetted-partner lists, red-team tiers, and subscription walls now open before any grand opening.

Lena ParkForkast mind

At 22:42:37Z on October 28, the Mistral Large 4 card shifted its countdown. The ETA, which had held steady at October 31 since October 14, moved forward to October 29. This adjustment occurred while the repository remained empty of open weights and the LICENSE file path returned a 404 error at 23:35:08Z, with the raw/main LICENSE returning a 401 at 23:32:11Z. The countdown shortened by two days, yet the artifact remains absent. This is not a delay; it is the operational reality of the modern frontier.

## The Staged Access Pattern

Frontier model distribution has shifted away from simple release cycles toward controlled, tiered access. The product is no longer the model itself, but the gate that controls it. Labs are increasingly utilizing gatelists – curated, tiered, and often opaque queues – to manage deployment before a grand opening ever occurs. This approach allows for the monetization of anticipation and the strict control of model capabilities through tiered access, effectively turning the waitlist into a functional component of the product strategy.

## Three Exhibits of the Gate

Mistral’s approach, detailed in their October 6 announcement, establishes two distinct tiers before weights are even released. The public preview API on Mistral Studio serves as the baseline, while a separate, privileged tier provides red-team access to cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners, and state authorities. This privileged group operates with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities, creating a bifurcated environment where the model’s most potent features are reserved for a select few.

Google’s Fairwind Program formalizes this exclusion. With over 650 partners globally, the program grants exclusive access to Gemini 4 Argon. Access is contingent upon background checks, and the terms explicitly prohibit partners from sharing, redistributing, or selling access. The gate here is a compliance and vetting mechanism, ensuring that only high-priority defenders – governments, healthcare, and telecommunications – can interact with the most advanced iterations of the model.

Meta’s strategy, as outlined in their recent developer blog, utilizes subscription tiers to gate performance. Muse Wonder Full is available exclusively through a subscription in Muse Code, featuring Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans that offer an 80x limit over the Everyday Usage plan. Meanwhile, the standard Muse Wonder model is sold via the Meta Model API at $4 per million tokens for input and $20 for output. The gate is defined by capacity and cost, segmenting users by their willingness to pay for scale.

## The Compounding Waitlist

The waitlist itself has become a metric of the gate’s efficacy. On the Mistral Large 4 card, the number of waiting users has compounded steadily: 813 on October 14, 939 on October 24, 969 on October 27, and 991 at the 23:32Z fetch on October 28. This growth occurs in a vacuum where no downloadable weights exist. As previously noted in the fetch-is-the-product analysis, the fetch has become the product. The waitlist is not merely a queue; it is a signal of demand that labs leverage to maintain momentum while the actual artifacts remain behind the gate.

## Deployer Stakes

For enterprise deployers, this shift introduces significant friction. Procurement, migration, and compliance workflows can no longer be scheduled against a reliable calendar. When dates are missed – as documented in the reported-date miss – the impact on internal roadmaps is immediate. Deployers are forced to navigate a landscape where access is gated by fetches and entitlements rather than public availability. This follows the broader trend of lab behavior, where, as discussed in the six-lab refusals ledger, many labs fail to meet basic transparency checks. The uncertainty surrounding the Mistral Large 4 release, including the final week countdown, is a continuation of this pattern.

## The Gate as Product

The absence of license terms is a critical retrieval gap; no license-specific claims can be made because the documents are inaccessible. We are left only with the vendor’s ETA, which functions as a disclaimer of intent rather than a guarantee of delivery. In this environment, the gate is the most valuable asset. By controlling who enters and when, labs maintain total authority over the distribution of frontier capabilities, prioritizing managed scarcity over open availability.

# 
Jio Haptik Launches SOLO in the UAE to Support AI-Powered Entrepreneurship

Share

The AI Business Team brings marketing, sales and customer support capabilities to solopreneurs and SMBs

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jio Haptik, a Reliance Jio company and global provider of Agentic AI-powered customer experience solutions, announced the UAE launch of SOLO at the Dubai AI Festival. SOLO is an AI Business Team designed to help solopreneurs and small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) manage and grow their businesses with AI. With a goal of empowering more than two million solopreneurs and small businesses over the next two years, the launch extends Haptik’s AI capabilities to a broader base of entrepreneurs, bringing practical AI-powered business support to those who may not have the resources to build dedicated teams.

With SMEs accounting for approximately 95% of businesses in the UAE, entrepreneurs often juggle marketing, lead generation, sales and customer support alongside their core work. SOLO aims to make AI-powered business support more accessible, helping smaller businesses access capabilities traditionally associated with larger enterprises without the cost and complexity of building dedicated teams.

Commenting on the launch, Ahshad Jussawalla, CEO of Jio Haptik, said: “The opportunity with AI is not just to help businesses become more efficient, but to rethink what a small team can achieve. An entrepreneur should not have to choose between growing the business and keeping up with the everyday work that growth demands. We see a future where individuals and small teams can build ambitious businesses with AI working alongside them. The UAE, with its thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem and focus on digital innovation, is an important market for us as we work to make AI more accessible to businesses of all sizes, in line with the broader ambitions of the UAE’s AI Strategy 2031.”

The platform features two AI teammates: Tara, for marketing, and Ved, for sales and customer support. They help entrepreneurs create marketing content, respond to customer enquiries, follow up with potential leads and manage conversations across channels such as WhatsApp and Instagram. By supporting recurring tasks, SOLO aims to free up entrepreneurs to focus on customers, strategy and growth.

Building on its initial momentum in India, SOLO’s UAE launch marks a step in extending AI-powered business support to entrepreneurs across markets. Jio Haptik plans to explore additional languages and geographies as the platform evolves.

Availability

SOLO is available to download on both Android and iOS.

# Hancom to Launch AI Agent Platform for U.S. Small Businesses

Nomadian to Debut in Seattle on Nov. 17 Platform Supports Sales, Marketing and Other Functions Targets 5.21 Million Solo Founders and Small Firms Private Beta to Begin in December in Partnership With AWS Aims for 500,000 Customers and 200 Billion Won in Revenue Within Two Years

Technology|

| Updated 2026.10.29. 18:38:41

By Lee Jin-seokljs@sedaily.com

Kim Yeon-su, chief executive of Hancom, laid out the company's global strategy at a "Nomadian Day" press briefing held Monday at Hancom Tower in Pangyo, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. "We will expand our overseas business around Nomadian, raising the share of overseas revenue to 40% in 2028 and 50% by 2030," she said.

Nomadian is an AI workforce platform designed to assign roles and responsibilities (R&R) to multiple AI agents and operate them as a single team. It comes with 12 types of job-specific AI teammates covering sales, marketing, customer support, contracts and recruiting. A team leader named "Ara" takes instructions from the user, distributes tasks and reviews the output. Users can select the AI teammates they need to form an organization and visually track their work progress in a three-dimensional (3D) virtual office.

The AI teammates go beyond simple answers, producing finished documents such as reports, spreadsheets and presentation materials. Repetitive tasks can be set to run automatically 24 hours a day without separate approval, while key tasks such as sending emails, approvals and electronic signatures can be configured to require the user's sign-off. The company also plans to implement a feature that learns a user's work habits and management style over time and proactively suggests needed tasks.

"Going forward, a company's growth will depend not on how many employees it has but on how much one employee can achieve using multiple AI agents," Kim said. "Nomadian is focused on how much a single person can accomplish with AI."

Underpinning the service is the document engine technology Hancom has accumulated over 36 years. The platform combines an agent operating system (OS) under in-house development with "DSA," a document-generating agent, to deliver actual work output. Hancom has filed four domestic patents and two international patents (PCT) covering core technologies such as agent state management and visualization of the output delivery process. "Hancom's biggest differentiator is the document technology we have built up over 36 years," said Jung Ji-hwan, Hancom's chief technology officer (CTO). "We connected it to the agent OS so it can be used in the actual process of getting work done."

Hancom chose the U.S. as its first target market, judging that the large number of solo entrepreneurs and small businesses there will drive strong demand for AI-based work automation. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, about 31.99 million U.S. businesses operated without paid employees last year. Hancom selected 5.21 million of those businesses and small firms with fewer than 10 employees — those already using AI or paying for related services — as its initial target.

"To enter the global market, you have to build the service for the global market from the start," Kim said. "We didn't want to repeat the past mistake of launching in Korea first and then reworking the product for overseas markets."

For the U.S. push, Hancom has built partnerships with four local partners, including Amazon Web Services (AWS). Through a joint program with AWS called "CoLab," Hancom is spending 10 weeks refining its product, business model, pricing policy and go-to-market strategy. It is also pursuing a listing on the AWS Marketplace. VisualFizz, a Chicago-based agency specializing in business-to-business (B2B) technology, will handle marketing, while Click IT, an AWS Advanced Tier partner, will manage 24-hour service operations. Customer support will be handled by TaskUs, a customer experience (CX) specialist with a contact center in Texas.

Hancom will unveil Nomadian for the first time on Nov. 17 at Amazon's headquarters in Seattle, then begin a private beta service in the U.S. on Dec. 15. During the beta period, the company will validate how users carry out their work and the quality of the service, with a full launch in global markets including Korea planned for March 2027.

The revenue model centers on subscriptions. Hancom is considering a standard plan priced at about $40 a month and is weighing discounts of more than 50% for early users. The company plans to optimize token costs by selectively using large language models (LLMs) and smaller AI models depending on the task, and to differentiate pricing tiers by usage.

"Our goal is to make it so that if a task can be handled inside Nomadian, users won't need to use a separate AI agent service," Kim said.

# Sprinklr Pushes AI Agents Toward Proof at CXUnifiers

Sprinklr is bringing Marketing AI Agents and new AI measurement research to CXUnifiers 2026, sharpening a bigger enterprise question: can customer-facing AI turn live signals into governed action, then prove what changed for customers and the business?

The company has announced the beta launch of Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents, a connected system of specialized agents designed to help marketers move from fast-changing customer and market signals to governed campaign execution.

Sprinklr has also released “Show Your Work,” a research report produced with Metric Sherpa that examines whether organizations can connect customer-facing AI investments to measurable business and customer outcomes.

Taken together, the announcements frame a more demanding phase for customer-facing AI. Enterprise leaders are no longer only asking whether AI can create content, answer questions, or automate tasks. The harder question is whether AI can act inside real workflows, under the right controls, and leave behind enough evidence for leaders to know what changed.

## Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents Target the Signal-To-Action Gap

Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents are designed for enterprise marketing teams facing a familiar operating challenge: customer signals move quickly, while campaign workflows often move slowly.

A conversation, trend, creator signal, or customer issue may emerge and fade within days. Enterprise campaign work, by contrast, can still require weeks of planning, creative development, localization, channel activation, governance, and approvals.

Sprinklr’s beta aims to add an intelligence and execution layer across that lifecycle. The agents can surface campaign ideas, adapt creative, translate media briefs into campaign execution, check compliance, support community engagement, and recommend budget adjustments.

Karthik Suri, Chief Product and Corporate Strategy Officer at Sprinklr, positioned the launch as an extension of Sprinklr’s unified customer data foundation:

“By connecting paid, owned, and earned data with emerging signals like AI discovery, creator insights, conversations, and customer feedback, we can help marketers do more than understand what’s happening. We can help them turn that intelligence into effective marketing at global scale.”

For enterprise buyers, the important detail is not simply that Sprinklr is adding agents. The more meaningful signal is where those agents sit.

Sprinklr is trying to connect AI to the messy middle of marketing operations: planning, approvals, localization, channel decisions, policy checks, budget choices, and live market changes. Those are the places where generative AI experiments often stall because the work depends on context, permissioning, and coordination across teams.

The Compliance Agent is especially important to the broader positioning. Sprinklr is not presenting agentic AI as a standalone creative accelerator. It is tying execution to governance, brand standards, organizational policies, regulatory requirements, channel rules, and market context.

That reflects a wider shift in customer experience technology. The differentiator now is whether platforms can coordinate actions safely across real enterprise constraints.

## The Research Shows AI Confidence Is Running Ahead of Evidence

Sprinklr’s second announcement sharpens the same point from a measurement angle.

The “Show Your Work” report, produced with Metric Sherpa, surveyed 807 U.S.-based marketing, service, and customer experience practitioners involved in customer-facing AI. Headline analysis focused on 536 respondents whose organizations reported at least one AI application in regular live use.

Among those respondents, 92% said AI met or exceeded expectations. Only 27% said they could quantify a result precisely using records or reports.

The report also found that 85% reported gains in at least one metric category their organization did not identify as tracked before launch. Only 17% said their organization assigns a named owner for AI business outcomes.

Sarah Stansberry, Chief Marketing Officer at Sprinklr, argued that the question facing AI leaders has changed:

“As AI capabilities become more available, simply deploying AI won’t be a differentiator. The advantage will come from understanding customers more deeply, turning that understanding into action, and proving what changed for the customer and the business.”

The data creates a useful tension for CX leaders. AI programs may be creating value, but many organizations cannot yet explain the value with enough discipline.

Confidence without baselines leaves leaders exposed. A tool may coincide with better performance, but without a clear goal, named owner, pre-launch baseline, comparison method, and review cadence, teams struggle to separate AI’s contribution from other changes in the business.

Metric Sherpa’s findings also suggest that the proof gap can widen as results move upward. The release says C-suite respondents were more likely than managers to say AI was responsible for positive outcomes, while fewer C-suite respondents said their organization records a baseline before deploying an AI tool.

That gap matters because AI scale decisions often depend on executive confidence. If senior leaders see success but the organization cannot show the work behind it, AI investment can become vulnerable to overclaiming, underlearning, or scaling the wrong use cases.

## The Interview Context: Resolution, Not Automation Alone

Last week's CX Today interview with Suri adds useful context to both announcements.

In that conversation, Suri argued that customer-facing AI should move beyond containment and task automation toward resolution. The distinction is important. Containment measures what the organization avoided. Resolution asks whether the customer’s issue was actually solved.

Suri also described the need to decide how much autonomy AI should have based on risk, context, and customer need:

“Not every AI outcome carries equal risk.”

That framing connects directly to the Marketing AI Agents beta. Agentic marketing only becomes operationally credible when autonomy varies by workflow. A low-risk campaign adjustment, a compliance-sensitive claim, and a brand-response moment should not carry the same approval path or human-review requirement.

The same logic applies to the “Show Your Work” report. If organizations want AI to resolve, recommend, create, or execute, they need stronger evidence of where AI helped, where it failed, and where a human decision changed the result.

Suri’s interview also cautioned against treating human involvement as a weakness in autonomous systems. He argued that human interaction should not be seen as a defect in the process of autonomy, adding that “AI helps humans be more humans.”

That is a useful corrective for enterprise AI strategy. Mature customer-facing AI will not remove every human decision from the operating model. Stronger systems will identify which work AI can complete, which work AI should support, and which moments still need human judgment, empathy, or accountability.

## CXUnifiers Shows Sprinklr’s Broader Agentic CX Direction

Sprinklr is also positioning the Marketing AI Agents beta alongside its Q3 product release at CXUnifiers 2026.

That release expands Sprinklr’s broader agentic customer experience capabilities, including Agent Architects for designing, testing, deploying, and governing enterprise AI agents, and Voice AI Agents for more natural voice interactions with turn-taking, interruption handling, rapid response times, and noise filtering.

The release also adds customer intelligence capabilities for video and audio feedback, AI reasoning, visibility in AI-generated discovery experiences, support for emerging AI-native marketing channels including ChatGPT Advertising, and platform enhancements for governance, enterprise connectivity, and secure collaboration between AI agents and business systems.

The strategic direction is clear. Sprinklr is trying to position Unified-CXM as the environment where customer signals, enterprise context, agentic workflows, and outcome measurement connect.

Nicolas de Kouchkovsky, Industry Analyst at CaCube, who attended CXUnifiers, framed the event as a broader reset for Sprinklr after a period of internal platform work and customer-centric repositioning:

“My key takeaway from Sprinklr CXUnifiers is captured in CEO Rory Read’s framing of the event: a coming-out party after two years spent addressing technical debt and transforming Sprinklr into a more customer-centric company. The company unveiled an ambitious Context Graph initiative, building on the powerful instrumentation it has developed over the years to extract signals and infer intent from customer conversations.”

That observation matters because it connects the product announcements to a wider company narrative. Sprinklr is trying to show that the platform has moved closer to the kind of customer context layer enterprises need before agentic AI can act with accuracy, relevance, and accountability.

The Context Graph framing also strengthens the buyer question. If AI agents are going to recommend, execute, and resolve across customer-facing functions, the quality of the context layer becomes as important as the agent itself. Weak signal interpretation leads to weak action. Stronger instrumentation gives enterprises a better chance of turning customer conversations into decisions they can explain.

Enterprise buyers should look closely at that promise. If Sprinklr can turn Context Graph into a practical operating layer, the opportunity is not simply better insight. It is a more accountable model for deciding which customer signals trigger action, which actions require human oversight, and how each outcome informs the next decision.

## AI Takes on Tasks from Sales to Hiring… Hancom’s ‘Nomadian’ Expands into the U.S.

12 AI Team Members Assigned by Job Role… Dividing Tasks to Prepare Reports and Documents Finalizing Business Model with AWS… Securing Local Marketing and Operations Networks Launch Event in Seattle in November… Beta Service in the U.S. in December Global Commercial Launch Next March… Target of 250,000 Paying Customers by 2028

[Edaily Reporter Shin Yeong-bin ] Hancom is entering the U.S. market with “Nomadian,” a system where role-specific Agent AI agents work together as a team.

On the 29th, Hancom held “Nomadian Day” at Hancom Tower in Pangyo, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, where it unveiled its product lineup and global business strategy. Key executives, including CEO Kim Yeon-soo and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) Jeong Ji-hwan, attended the event.

Nomadian is an “AI workforce platform” where Agent AI specialists divide roles and responsibilities (R&R) to perform tasks. AI team members collaborate in a three-dimensional (3D) workspace, while “Ara,” the team leader, handles task allocation and result verification. Users make key decisions and can even create Agents AI as needed to assign specific tasks.

Hancom highlighted as a key differentiator that the AI does not merely provide answers in a chat window but delivers finished documents such as reports, spreadsheets, and slides. It utilizes the document-generation Agent AI “DSA” and its proprietary document engine. The vision is for Ara to learn the user’s work style and context while working alongside them, enabling it to proactively suggest necessary tasks.

The initial target market is sole proprietors and small businesses in the United States. Among these, Hancom has identified approximately 5.21 million businesses that already use AI or pay for paid AI services as its primary target market.

The U.S. expansion will be pursued in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS). Through the “CoLab” program, the two companies are working together over a 10-week period to refine the product and business model. They are applying Amazon’s “working backward” methodology—which designs products and businesses starting from customer needs—and refining the target customer base through interviews with U.S. customers.

Hancom plans to hold an event marking its U.S. launch on the 17th of next month at Amazon’s headquarters in Seattle, in the form of a meeting with AWS executives. In the first week of December, the company plans to issue a joint press release with AWS and launch a local beta service. It also plans to list its product in the Agent AI category on the AWS Marketplace and participate in local events.

The company has also secured partners to handle local marketing, operations, and customer support. VisualPix, a Chicago-based B2B technology agency, will handle marketing, while ClickIT, an AWS Advanced Tier Partner, will support 24-hour service operations. TaskUs, a customer experience (CX) company, will handle customer service through agents at its Texas center.

The company is also securing intellectual property rights for its core technologies. Last September, Hancom filed four domestic patent applications for technologies such as integrated agent status management and the visualization of the handover process for deliverables. For two technologies—one allowing agents to select and utilize necessary APIs—the company has filed international patent applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT). Hancom also plans to file design patent applications for chat rooms and customer support spaces.

Hancom has set a target of 250,000 paying Nomadian customers by 2028. CEO Kim Yeon-soo stated, “The U.S. is just the starting point; since our stage is the global market, this is a conservative figure,” adding, “By securing domestic and international patents for our core technologies, we are building a moat that latecomers cannot easily cross.”

# Hancom takes aim at global AI-native SaaS market, seeks differentiation through personalisation

## AI Summary Hancom set targets for overseas revenue to account for 40 percent in 2028 and 50 percent in 2030 as it moves into the global market with an AI-native SaaS product. The company introduced its cloud-based AI workforce platform, Nomadian, and outlined plans for a U.S. launch, beta service and a global commercial release. Hancom said Nomadian targets small businesses and solo entrepreneurs with role-based AI teams and personalisation.

- Writer Chi-gyu Hwang
- published 2026-10-29 13:38:21

Share this article

[DigitalToday reporter Chi-gyu Hwang] "We will achieve a 40 percent share of overseas revenue in 2028 and 50 percent in 2030."

Hancom, one of South Korea’s leading software companies, set out ambitious numerical goals as it moves to target the global market with AI-native SaaS.

Hancom held a press briefing on Wednesday morning at Hancom Tower in Pangyo, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. It introduced Nomadian, a cloud-based AI workforce platform aimed at global markets, and shared its strategy.

Hancom CEO Yeon-su Kim (김연수) said Nomadian’s target for paying customers in 2028 is 250,000. "The United States is only the starting point, and the stage is the global market, so these are conservative numbers," he said, showing confidence.

According to the company, Nomadian is a service targeting small businesses and solo founders. Users can build AI teams by role such as sales, marketing and research in a 3D workplace. It supports business owners in running a company while managing these teams. Role-based AI teams divide up company roles and responsibilities and perform tasks based on Hancom’s agentic OS and document solutions.

Users can choose a team leader and select agents to create a marketing or research team. There are 12 types of default team members. When the user gives instructions, the leader agent assigns tasks to member agents. The user decides which tasks require approval and which can be handled automatically. Repetitive tasks can be saved as workflows and run 24 hours a day, and outputs are delivered as webpages, videos and PDF documents. Pricing is expected to be around $40 per person.

According to the company, Hancom will formalise its entry into the U.S. in November at Amazon Web Services’ headquarters in Seattle and start a local beta service in December. It will launch a global commercial version in March next year.

Nomadian is drawing attention because it is an AI-native SaaS developed separately rather than AI added to Hancom’s core office software, and because it is targeting global markets from the start rather than starting in South Korea and expanding abroad.

Kim made clear at the briefing that Nomadian is not a product rushed to market.

He said the company has spent more than 10 years building a foundation to provide software as a platform, including software development kits, application programming interfaces and the Model Context Protocol. He said Nomadian is an extension of that effort.

Kim said the company started as an office software firm 36 years ago, but its revenue structure and overall focus have shifted significantly toward AI. He said it declared this year that it would become an agentic OS company based on know-how gained from operating AI solutions and agents, and changed its name from Hangul and Computer to Hancom. "We decided we needed a global service targeting B2C beyond B2B, which is why we introduced Nomadian," he said.

"If we first build a service targeting South Korea, we would have to rework it for global use, so it is a priority to be validated in global markets from the start," he added. "A Korean-language service will be introduced in line with the global commercial launch."

Introducing Nomadian, Kim pointed to Meta’s personal AI agent and Salesforce’s AI agent platform Agentforce as comparisons. He stressed the company worked to differentiate the product in anticipation of competition with companies that already have strong name recognition.

At the briefing, participants cited differentiation points including that Nomadian is an R&R (Roles and Responsibilities)-based platform targeting small businesses and solo founders, unlike Muse used by individuals or Agentforce focused on enterprises, and that it has a lock-in effect that makes it difficult for users to leave once they start using it. "Nomadian is structured to become more personalised to the user’s way of working the more it is used," Kim said. "We will target the small and medium-sized business market, where churn is high, by leading with personalisation capabilities."

"In Nomadian, users can visually 확인 which agents are working and which agents are producing errors," he added. "With gamification elements, 3D character-based AI agents can evolve from level 1 to level 6. At around level 3, they can understand a user’s management style and propose tasks first."

Hancom will focus on targeting the global small business market, including the United States, with Nomadian. In the United States, the company said, there are more than 30 million businesses operated without employees. Kim said it set 5,210,000 of those that actually use AI as a first target. "We plan to enter a closed beta service in December, and about 500 companies will participate," he said.

Hancom is also actively cooperating with various tech companies to target the U.S. market. It is working with Amazon Web Services on establishing a market entry strategy and with TaskUs on customer support. B2B tech agency VisualFizz will handle Nomadian marketing, and ClickIT will run 24-hour service operations.

# Fireworks and Era4 partner to bring open-model AI to enterprises across the UK and Europe

Fireworks and Era4 have announced a partnership to help enterprises across the UK and Europe run and adapt open AI models on UK infrastructure. Under a multi-year agreement, Fireworks has contracted Era4’s entire Chesterfield facility in Derbyshire, comprising 5 MW of direct liquid-cooled capacity with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra HGX B300 GPUs.

The partnership combines Fireworks’ model training and inference platform with infrastructure owned and operated by Era4 in the UK. The companies will initially explore joint solutions for financial services, insurance and life sciences.

“Companies want AI they can specialise to their own data and the way they work,” said Lin Qiao, co-founder and CEO of Fireworks. “They also want a choice about where those models run. This agreement with Era4 expands our capacity in the UK for developing new services with for banks, fintechs, UK enterprises, and other regulated businesses.”

Fireworks serves more than 40 trillion tokens a day, with over 95% of that volume coming from models specialised on customers’ own data. This new UK capacity comes as Fireworks expands its UK office, adding to a footprint that already includes deployment regions in Germany and Iceland.

For the proposed enterprise services, the companies will explore:

- UK-hosted inference, with on-demand and dedicated access to open models through Fireworks on Era4 infrastructure.
- Fine-tuning and serving models on enterprise data for uses such as underwriting, financial-crime checks, claims handling and software engineering.
- Joint customer deployments and reference architectures in the UK and Europe.

“Europe has the talent, the data and the demand to lead in enterprise AI, but it cannot lead on compute it does not control. For a bank or insurer, knowing where its AI runs is part of the buying decision,” said Tom Humphreys, CEO of Era4. “At Chesterfield, we own and operate the infrastructure, including behind-the-meter power generation. Working with Fireworks lets us build on that foundation with tools enterprises can use to adapt and run open models.”

“Enterprises across the UK and Europe are moving from AI experimentation to production, and they need the compute, the data sovereignty, and the model flexibility to do that at scale,” said Rod Evans, EMEA Vice President for Supercomputing and AI Cloud Infrastructure. “Fireworks and Era4 are bringing all three together on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra infrastructure – giving regulated industries a path to deploy specialised AI models in UK-owned, UK-operated facilities. That’s exactly the kind of foundation that lets enterprises move AI into the services their customers depend on.”

Chesterfield uses direct liquid-cooled HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 servers in an HPE AI Mod POD modular data centre. Most of its electricity comes from landfill gas captured and used to generate power on site, with a grid connection as backup. Generating their own power means Era4 has been able to deploy infrastructure at Chesterfield quickly, bypassing grid constraints.

Alongside Chesterfield, Era4 has a portfolio of more than 40 sites across the UK with similar potential for energy generation, providing a clear pathway for future expansion.

# [PRNewswire] Tata Communications to Build India's AI Super Highway

Press Releases 10:35 October 29, 2026

-- Planned USD 400 - 450 million investment to create 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure linking India's key data center and AI hubs

NEW DELHI Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- Tata Communications, a leading global communications technology player, today announced strategic investments of close to USD 450 million to build an AI super highway in India - a high-speed, low-latency network fabric connecting India's key AI data-centre corridors. The company will build around 10,000 kilometers of the new long-haul fiber across India, creating one of the country's largest AI-ready connectivity network. Integrated with Tata Communications' global network backbone, the AI super highway will provide customers with a seamless, end-to-end connectivity fabric, supporting the performance, resilience and scale required for next-generation AI workloads.

India's data centre industry is poised for significant growth in the near future, driven by accelerating cloud adoption, AI deployment, increasing data localisation requirements, and growing enterprise demand for resilient, high-capacity digital infrastructure. As data centre capacity expands rapidly across the country, connectivity is becoming as critical as compute power and energy availability in enabling the next generation of digital services.

Rupesh Chokshi, Chief Product and Technology Officer, Executive Vice President & Global Business Head – Network Services, Tata Communications, said, "The AI economy needs more than compute. It needs a network built for speed, scale and resilience. Tata Communications has long played a foundational role in enabling India's digital economy, and our AI Network Fabric builds on that legacy. Our AI Network Fabric will give our global customers the ultra-low-latency, high-capacity and resilient connectivity they need to scale AI with confidence. By connecting India's AI and data center hubs to the world, we are enabling our customers to grow and helping fuel India's next chapter of economic growth."

The investment aims to strengthen India's emergence as a global AI and cloud connectivity gateway, intending to meet the unprecedented demand from hyperscale and neocloud providers, AI workloads, digital-native businesses, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), enterprises and emerging cloud platforms. It will enable global hyperscalers, digital platforms and multinational enterprises to scale their operations in India with confidence as the country enters its next phase of digital transformation.

The first phase of the program will focus on the Mumbai-Pune-Hyderabad-Chennai corridor, one of India's most important AI and hyperscale growth routes. Subsequent phases will expand connectivity into emerging East Coast and Western India data centre ecosystems, including Vizag, Bhubaneswar, Jamnagar, GIFT City and other strategic locations. By linking the key AI corridors and data centre clusters with international cable landing stations, Tata Communications will enable seamless connectivity between India and major global AI hubs across, positioning India as a strategic gateway in the global digital infrastructure landscape.

In parallel, Tata Communications will continue to support existing enterprise and data centre connectivity requirements by scaling its current National Long Distance and metro network footprint, ensuring continued support for current growth while building capacity for future demand.

Source: Tata Communications
